title: Make planning a real per-item pass that flags underspecified requests
summary: Replace the default-filled plan fields (rung defaulting to Implementation, first line as acceptance) with a planning pass that reads each open item against the brief, records and repository code. Items it can't specify are flagged and held back. The coordinated plan, with groups, order, flags and open questions, is viewable on demand. The audience is the user and the verifier, who judge whether the refusal gate now fires on real, vague requests.

defaults_applied.how: All changes are Rust code and tests.
Criteria require new passing tests, clean clippy and fmt.
Criteria check that vague items are refused and specified ones run, not that types exist.
The plan command must say explicitly when nothing is open or everything is refused.
The fix removes the defaults that disabled the gate (rung default, first-line acceptance), not just one instance.
Docs and the decision entry are written for an outside reader.
One focused change to the planning pass, the gate and the plan view.
The plan command is exercised through cargo run.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal and audience: the user wants the planning gate to be meaningful, so vague items are held back and flagged rather than run on defaults. The audience is the user, who sees the plan, and the verifier of this job.

'Actual planning pass' is read as a deterministic pass, with no new model role, over each item's request text, the brief, the job and proposal records, and file existence in the repository. A model-backed planner would be a new agent role and is out of this change. If the user wants one, they should say so.
Rung comes from the steward proposal if present, else is inferred from the request, reading and brief. If inference is not confident the item is flagged, not defaulted.
The view of the plan is a CLI command that prints text and JSON like other commands, plus the drain report. It does not need a web page.
The wiring of plan::trace and GapLog to the records is optional follow-up unless it is cheap. Tests for open_questions (the nit) are included.
The earlier verifier's note about display.rs being off-list is handled by listing display.rs here.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`: a new test shows an unread request with no bullets and no path-like words (for example 'make it better') is flagged underspecified. The flag names the missing field, and the item is not in Plan::order.
Run `cargo test`: a new test shows a request's first line is no longer copied into acceptance. Only explicit acceptance bullets, or a reading's criteria, fill it.

Run `cargo test`: a new test shows a non-proposal job's rung is inferred from its request or reading (for example docs/design work vs code), or flagged as missing. It is never silently set to Implementation, and an item with no determinable rung is refused.

Run `cargo test`: tests assert that open_questions are filled and checked for a read and an unread request. Questions include ambiguity found by the pass, such as a touched path that does not exist in the repository and an unresolved referenced job.
Run `cargo test`: a test shows two open items that name the same path get a dependency or are put in different groups. Items with disjoint touches are grouped together.

Run `cargo test`: a drain test using RealSteps over a records fixture with one specified and one vague queued item shows the vague one in Report::refused with a reason, and not run as a job. The specified one runs.

A user-invokable command (a new `athena plan` or equivalent, exercised with `cargo run`) prints the coordinated plan: order, parallel groups, each item's goal, rung, acceptance, open questions, dependencies and touches, and the flagged items with reasons. When nothing is open it says so explicitly instead of printing an empty success.

display.rs, main.rs and any other files touched outside plan.rs, reading.rs and drain.rs are named in the change's docs or decision entry. The tradeoff text in docs/decisions.md about the gate rarely firing is updated to describe the new behavior.
The change stays on the rust toolchain: `cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes. It uses no new secrets or personal data.
The docs say plainly whether the planning pass is deterministic code or calls a model, and whether the plan::trace and GapLog audit is wired to the records or still follow-up.

out_of_scope: Running plan groups concurrently; the drain stays one job at a time.
Moving compute to CI or any design work after the planning change.
A model-backed planner role or new prompts.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows or other governance files.
departures: The change touches the core plan, reading, drain, display and main files and adds a new command, so it is larger than the typical scored job. Cost, time and pass rate are shifted accordingly. The model-backed vs deterministic ambiguity also lowers reading acceptance.
